question: In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, pain and prolonged morning stiffness in scapular and pelvic girdles of several weeks of evolution that presents unilateral bruising of sudden onset, what treatment among the following would establish before confirming the diagnosis?

options.opb: Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Symptom evaluation -> Consider temporal artery biopsy -> 70% CHAIN: Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o. -> Rapid improvement in symptoms -> 80% CHAIN: Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days -> Faster onset of action compared to oral prednisone -> 75% CHAIN: Cyclophosphamide i.v. 1 g / m2 -> Reserved for specific conditions like severe lupus nephritis -> 60% CHAIN: Infliximab i.v. 3 mg / Kg -> Reserved for specific conditions like refractory rheumatoid arthritis -> 70%
analysis: Given the clinical presentation of a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, pain, prolonged morning stiffness in scapular and pelvic girdles, and unilateral bruising of sudden onset, the most appropriate initial treatment to consider before confirming the diagnosis would be a high-dose corticosteroid therapy to address potential inflammatory conditions such as giant cell arteritis or polymyalgia rheumatica.
